title: Injectivity into a product of localisations is equivalent to injectivity of the map multiplying by the elements
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For elements f_1, ..., f_n of a ring R and an R-module M, the lemma states that the map into the product of the localisations M_{f_i} is injective exactly when the map multiplying m by the tuple (f_1 m, ..., f_n m) is injective (statement lines 4621-4632). The proof does not compute with fractions: it rewrites the first condition as the statement that an element killed by powers of all the f_i vanishes, gets one direction immediately, and proves the converse by induction on the sum of the exponents, reducing in the induction step to a smaller total exponent by multiplying the element by one of the f_i (proof lines 4634-4648). The induction on the total exponent is the substance, and the author writes each step out. H2.
